title: Field-amplified readouts of weak altermagnetic exchange in MnF$_2$
authors: Guowen Jiang, Feilong Wang, Yunhua Wang, Fawei Zheng, Bin Xi, Hong-Gang Luo, Jize Zhao
abstract: MnF$_2$, the textbook two-sublattice antiferromagnet, has reemerged as a prototypical altermagnet, yet the sublattice-odd exchange that defines this identity remains under active debate: it enters the magnon splitting only in quadrature with the dipole--dipole interaction, its magnitude suppressed and its sign erased. An overdetermined first-principles total-energy mapping resolves this scale as a seventh-neighbor imbalance $δ{J_7}\simeq+8~μ$eV. The resulting Hamiltonian, with the dipole--dipole interaction included explicitly, reproduces the low-energy gap and the visible finite-momentum splitting. A longitudinal field $B\parallel c$ then acts as a linear amplifier of the hidden scale, opening two signed, field-linear readouts. The first is the compensation field $B^\ast(\mathbf Q)$, the position of minimum splitting, which is equal and opposite at the rotation-related partner momenta: a shift from zero field is itself evidence of a finite imbalance, its side gives the sign, and its magnitude, $|B^\ast|\simeq0.34$~T here, gives the scale. The second is the fixed-field contrast of the partner splittings, $\simeq0.14$~meV at $1$~T, six times the zero-field excess: a sign check from just two spectra. Both readouts survive a $0.12$~meV energy resolution, and the construction carries over to any easy-axis collinear altermagnet, bringing $μ$eV altermagnetic exchange within present instrumental reach.
summary: This study develops a method to measure the weak altermagnetic exchange coupling ($\delta J_7$) in $	ext{MnF}_2$ by exploiting its field-dependent magnetic excitations. By applying a longitudinal magnetic field, the authors linearize the readout, allowing the weak coupling to be determined from the shift of the minimum magnon splitting ($B^*$) or the field-linear contrast ($C(B)$). This technique proves that subtle, symmetry-related interactions can be brought into the reach of current experimental measurements.
main_problem: The paper aims to detect and quantify the weak, sublattice-odd exchange coupling ($\delta J_7$) that characterizes the altermagnetic nature of $	ext{MnF}_2$, as this signal is otherwise masked by dominant interactions at zero field.
main_result: The authors demonstrate two complementary, field-dependent readouts—the compensation field shift ($B^*$) and the fixed-field contrast ($C(B)$)—that linearly amplify the weak exchange scale, confirming its existence and magnitude ($\delta J_7 \simeq +8 \mu	ext{eV}$).
method: The analysis combines first-principles total-energy mapping to determine the coupling scale with theoretical modeling using linear spin-wave theory applied to the resulting effective Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{MnF}_2$, modeled as a two-sublattice antiferromagnet. The effective Hamiltonian includes Heisenberg exchange, long-range dipole-dipole interaction (DDI), and Zeeman coupling, analyzed via the bosonic Bogoliubov-de Gennes spectrum.
key_observables: The primary observables are the minimum splitting position $B^*(\mathbf{Q})$ (compensation field) and the field-dependent contrast $C(B) = \Omega_{\mathbf{A}}(B) - \Omega_{\mathbf{A}'}(B)$, both of which are linear in $\delta J_7$.
important_parameters: The key scale is the seventh-neighbor imbalance $\delta J_7 \simeq +8 \mu	ext{eV}$. The readouts are quantified by the compensation field $|B^*| \simeq 0.34 	ext{ T}$ and the fixed-field contrast $\simeq 0.14 	ext{ meV}$ at $1 	ext{ T}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the DDI dominates the visible fine structure, allowing the weak exchange to manifest as a measurable asymmetry amplified by an external longitudinal magnetic field.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structure of $	ext{MnF}_2$ and show the field dependence of the magnon splitting $\Omega(B)$, demonstrating the shift of the minimum splitting ($B^*$) and the linear, odd dependence of the contrast $C(B)$ on the applied field.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem (masked $\delta J_7$), develops the theoretical framework using symmetry relations and the BdG spectrum, proposes two field-dependent readouts ($B^*$ and $C(B)$), and finally presents calculations confirming the measurable, linear amplification of the weak exchange scale.
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated example of using external fields to linearize the measurement of a weak, symmetry-protected interaction, a concept applicable to detecting subtle couplings in complex quantum materials.

(a) Rutile magnetic cell with the two antiparallel Mn sublattices (Mn1 red, Mn2 blue), the F ions (green), and the near-neighbor exchange paths J1, J2, and J3; bold arrows indicate the an- tiparallel moments along the c axis. (b),(c) ab-plane projec- tion of the two seventh-neighbor paths as seen from sublattice Mn1 (b) and Mn2 (c). J7a and J7b have equal length and are interchanged by the spin-group operation [C2 ∥C4zτ] connect- ing the sublattices—hence the exchanged labels between the panels—but only J7b is bridged by two fluorine ions.

FIG. 2. Two-mode compensation mechanism, Eq. (5), for fixed D = 121.6 µeV and 2geffµB = 231.5 µeV/T. (a) δJ7 = 0 (Λ = 0), (b) QA, ΛA = +79.6 µeV, (c) QA′, ΛA′ = −79.6 µeV. In all panels the minimum floor equals D; the detuning only translates the minimum, to B∗= 0, −0.344 T, and +0.344 T (dashed lines). Panel (a) is the null case, the minimum pinned at B = 0; panels (b) and (c) re- alize the two partner momenta of MnF2 at a common field, and their fixed-field difference is the directly measurable sign contrast.
